newsitem.title: POLAND: Metro sees 1998 Polish sales over DM 1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Metro sees 1998 Polish sales over DM 1 bln.

text.p: German retailing group Metro AG, which signed a joint-venture deal with Polish Bank Handlowy on Wednesday, expects next year's sales in its Polish units to amount to one billion marks, Metro's president said.
"Next year probably we will have more than one-billion-mark sales in Poland," Klaus Wiegandt told Reuters.

Wiegandt said Metro's Polish sales this year have so far reached 250 million marks. The firm is now represented in Poland by its Vobis Microcomputer Sp.zoo, Tip Discount Polska Sp.zoo, Praktiker Polska Sp.zoo and Real Sp.zoo chains.
Wiegandt also said the company did not expect any profits in the near future as it would spend a lot on staff training and infrastructure.
"We will not have any profits in the nearest future because we have a lot of staff to train and we have to develop our infrastructure," Wiegandt said.

Under a joint venture agreement signed on Wednesday between Metro AG and Bank Handlowy, the bank would take over a 25-percent stake in Metro's Polish units of Real and Tip Discount worth 43 million marks.
Handlowy's president told Reuters it was a long-term investment and it would bear fruit within the next five years.
"We have three- and five-year investment portfolios. This investment should produce a return after three years," Cezary Stypulkowski said.
Stypulkowski also said the purchase of the stake is a first step towards issuing shares in the Polish Metro units which would take place within three to five years.
